name: Interferon alpha hair texture change

lead: Interferon alfa is a prescription medicine used with ribavirin for chronic hepatitis C. Doctors have reported that some patients' hair texture changed during treatment, with naturally curly hair turning straight, or in other reports straight hair turning curly.

A 2002 letter in the British Journal of Dermatology described two HIV-negative patients with naturally curly hair who developed complete straightening on interferon alfa-2b plus ribavirin. In one, the curls returned after the drug was stopped and the change recurred when it was restarted [1].

paras: This is not a cosmetic method. It has been described only as an effect noticed by patients receiving medically prescribed interferon treatment under a doctor's care.

Interferon-based treatment carries significant side effects, and the hair report also noted diffuse scalp thinning, increased grey hair and eyebrow lengthening in one patient [1]. It is available only by prescription for medical indications.

angle.text: Some patients treated with interferon saw their hair become straight or curly. It is a medical side effect that has been documented in case reports, not a routine way to change hair texture.

lead: Hair texture change with interferon alpha refers to reports that patients receiving interferon alfa, usually with ribavirin for chronic hepatitis C, noticed a change in hair form, most often straightening of naturally curly hair and, in other case reports, new curling.[1]

In the best-known report, a 2002 letter by Bessis and colleagues in the British Journal of Dermatology, two HIV-negative patients with naturally curly hair developed acquired straightening on interferon alfa-2b with ribavirin. The first patient, a 58-year-old man who started treatment in January 1999, had rough, straw-like hair on the scalp and body, diffuse thinning, more grey hair and longer eyebrows.[1] After treatment stopped, his curly hair regrew spontaneously and the eyebrow change regressed, with normalisation complete about two months later; the changes recurred identically when pegylated interferon and ribavirin were restarted.[1]

The topic appears in hair-texture discussion because it shows that a drug can change hair form, but the reports describe a side effect that, in the documented case, reversed once the drug was stopped.

paras: The 2002 letter called the straightening a curious, previously unreported manifestation in two patients with naturally curly hair.[1] In the first patient the change was reversible after stopping the drug and recurred on rechallenge.[1]
No studies found beyond case reports and small observational series on hair changes during interferon and ribavirin treatment, including the 2002 letter.[1]
